name: App launch
objective: The application starts and shows the sign-in entry without blocking errors.
expectedOutcomes: Sign-in screen renders with email, password and register entry
No uncaught JavaScript errors or failed app-shell requests
authorization: No protected data visible before authentication

name: Clinic-owner registration
objective: A new clinic owner can register, and the registration contract (including Idempotency-Key) is honoured.
testData: Synthetic owner and clinic from the identity factory
expectedOutcomes: Client-side validation rejects empty/invalid input
Valid submission succeeds and lands on a post-registration screen
Registration status endpoint reports a lifecycle status for the new applicant
Replaying the same request payload with the same key does not create a second applicant
authorization: Registration status is readable only by the authenticated applicant
Missing Idempotency-Key is rejected by the backend
persistence: Application record exists server-side and survives reload

backend.note: API-level checks: header requirement, unauthenticated status, replay

name: Login
objective: The registered owner authenticates and reaches an authenticated area showing their identity.
expectedOutcomes: Valid credentials sign in
Invalid credentials are rejected with a visible error
Authenticated area identifies the signed-in account (or its clinic)
authorization: Wrong password never yields a session
persistence: Token issued by the configured auth provider

name: Session persistence
objective: The session is restored after a browser reload (web) or backgrounding/resume (Android) without re-entering credentials.
expectedOutcomes: Protected screen remains accessible after reload/resume
Cleared storage returns the user to sign-in
authorization: Protected routes are not accessible without a session
persistence: Session storage only; no clinical data cached for signed-out users

name: Clinic onboarding
objective: The owner completes the applicable onboarding journey and the clinic information is saved.
expectedOutcomes: Onboarding journey reachable after sign-in according to application status
Entered clinic information is persisted and shown again after reload
authorization: Only the owner can modify their own clinic onboarding
productRuleGaps: Manual-review versus automatic approval depends on the backend auto-approval engine; the policy (automatic-approval-first) must be preserved, not asserted beyond observed status.

name: Dashboard and role-based navigation
objective: The signed-in user sees a dashboard with navigation appropriate to their role; unauthorized routes and actions are rejected.
expectedOutcomes: Dashboard renders for the role
Role-specific navigation entries only
Direct navigation to an unauthorized route is refused or redirected
authorization: Backend rejects calls outside the role (401/403) irrespective of UI hiding

name: Patient creation and search
objective: A synthetic patient can be created, found by search and reopened with persisted details.
expectedOutcomes: Patient appears in list and search
Opened record shows saved details
authorization: Patient visible only inside the owning clinic

name: Appointment creation and details
objective: An appointment for the test patient can be created and is visible in the schedule and detail view.
expectedOutcomes: Create succeeds and navigates to the appointment detail
Appointment visible in list/schedule with correct patient and time
authorization: Cross-clinic access denied

name: Consultation and case sheet
objective: Starting a consultation attaches an episode and a case sheet that persist clinical information.
expectedOutcomes: Episode created/attached to the appointment
Case sheet saved and reopened with the same content
Case sheet belongs to the same episode and patient
authorization: Only authorized clinical roles can edit the case sheet
productRuleGaps: A doctor account for the test clinic must exist; creating one requires staff onboarding UI/API not yet automated.

name: Prescription and treatment
objective: Prescription and treatment recommendation/scheduling work according to specialty configuration and permissions.
expectedOutcomes: Prescription can be created in the supported workflow
Treatment recommendation and scheduling only where the clinic supports it
authorization: Doctor recommends; admin schedules (existing responsibility split)

android.note: Depends on Expo Go + Maestro feasibility

name: Restart and data persistence
objective: Saved records persist across reload (web) or relaunch (Android).
expectedOutcomes: Patient, appointment and clinical record are present after reload/relaunch
authorization: n/a

name: Logout and login again
objective: Logout ends the session and denies protected access; signing in again restores the same identity and records.
expectedOutcomes: Logout returns to sign-in
Protected route is denied after logout
Re-login shows same account and saved records
authorization: No residual access after logout

name: Ayurveda clinic onboarding
objective: An Ayurveda clinic owner registers and completes onboarding; Ayurveda specialty configuration persists and drives Ayurveda-specific sections and therapy navigation.
expectedOutcomes: Clinic type persisted as ayurveda
Ayurveda assessment sections and therapy navigation available
Configuration unchanged after reload and re-login
authorization: Specialty configuration is read from the backend, never assumed by the test

name: General clinic onboarding
objective: A General clinic owner registers and completes onboarding; Ayurveda-specific sections and therapy appointment creation are absent while ordinary appointments and consultations work.
expectedOutcomes: Clinic type persisted as general
No Ayurveda-specific sections
No therapy appointment option
Ordinary appointment and consultation unaffected
Configuration unchanged after reload and re-login
authorization: Direct route and API access cannot bypass the restriction (see gaps)
productRuleGaps: Backend enforcement of the General-clinic therapy restriction at the appointment-creation endpoint is not evident in the source; see NC-UAT-17.

name: Ayurveda therapy appointment creation
objective: In an Ayurveda clinic a therapy appointment (with therapist/resource, date, start, duration) can be created and persists.
preconditions: Ayurveda clinic with a therapist and a patient
expectedOutcomes: Therapy appointment saved with therapist, date, start and duration
Visible in schedule and detail; persists after reload
authorization: Only authorized roles can create
productRuleGaps: A therapist staff member for the test clinic must exist.

name: Therapy scheduling conflict simulation
objective: Overlap and boundary behaviour for therapist/resource and patient conflicts follows the implemented rules.
expectedOutcomes: Overlap for the same therapist is rejected or reported as conflict
Non-overlapping appointment for same therapist is accepted
Overlapping appointments for the same patient are rejected or reported
Back-to-back (second starts exactly when first ends) is accepted: ranges are half-open
Different therapist and patient with overlapping time is accepted
authorization: n/a
persistence: Accepted appointments persist; rejected create no record

backend.note: Comprehensive predicates verified from source and via compiled SQL

productRuleGaps: Whether a conflict is blocking (409/validation error) or warning-only for single appointment creation must be confirmed at runtime; the SQL predicates are strict half-open (start < other end AND end > other start).

name: General clinic therapy restriction
objective: A General clinic cannot schedule therapy appointments through navigation, direct routes or the API, and no record is created.
expectedOutcomes: No therapy scheduling option in navigation
Direct route is refused or redirected
API attempt with a General identity is rejected
No therapy appointment record exists afterwards
authorization: Backend specialty/authorization enforcement is mandatory
productRuleGaps: Backend enforcement to be confirmed; if absent this is a product-rule/implementation gap, not a test failure to be hidden.

name: Cross-clinic specialty and data isolation
objective: Each clinic sees only its own patients, appointments, therapy records and clinical data; switching accounts leaks no permissions or cached data.
preconditions: Ayurveda and General clinics with data
expectedOutcomes: Ayurveda clinic sees its own therapy appointments
General clinic does not see Ayurveda records
Cross-tenant ID access is denied
After switching accounts no previous clinic data or permissions are shown
authorization: Tenant isolation enforced by the backend

name: Server-side access-token revocation
objective: Logout revokes the session on the server: a token captured from the browser stops working, refresh cannot restore it, and the user's other sessions stay valid.
expectedOutcomes: An independent second session of the same user can call the API before logout
A token captured from the browser works before logout
Logout returns to sign-in
Replaying the captured token after logout is rejected as session_revoked (401)
Reload and direct navigation to /clinic-admin, /profile and /onboarding/wizard-flow show sign-in
A token minted by refreshing the revoked session, if one is issued, is rejected (401)
The independent second session still works after logout
authorization: A captured access token has no residual access after logout and cannot be restored by refresh
persistence: Revocation applies to the signed-out session only; other sessions of the same user are unaffected

web.note: Captured browser token replayed against the API

android.note: No Android flow for this scenario yet

manual-android.note: No manual Android procedure defined yet
